title: Edge capacity decision log — region tradeoffs and small-batch reserve
content:
Meeting: Edge capacity decision huddle
Date: 2027-06-14
Attendees: Amira Kline (notes), Diego Park, Rina Patel, Marcus Li, Omar Bennett, + on-call SRE (TBD)
Context / why this doc: capture the rationale behind this week’s proposal to maintain a small reserved pool in edge regions for low-latency customers and for fast failover when central regions are saturated. We need a short, traceable decision log for later retro and for sales/solutions questions.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Proposal accepted (soft): keep 6–8 GPUs reserved per high-demand edge region (US-WEST-2 edge POP, EU-CENTRAL-1 edge POP) for small-batch / low-latency traffic and emergency spill. Use prewarmed lightweight VLAN nodes (lower VCPU profile) to reduce spin-up time.
- Tradeoffs: small cost increase (~4–6% regional infra spend) vs measured 30–40 ms tail reduction for 95th-99th percentile latency for <128-token requests.
- Short-term runway: trial for 6 weeks, evaluate using the edge-sla-metrics dashboard; automatic rollback if cost delta >8% or if 95p latency improvement <15% after 3 weeks.

Notes from discussion:
1) Problem framing
- Observed incidents in May: 3 x cross-region failovers where primary region hit prewarming latency cliffs (tickets JIRA-2987, JIRA-3052). In all cases, customers with strict latency SLOs experienced 200–600 ms spikes while we spun up capacity.
- Current solutions: central prewarmed pools + regional autoscale. Central pools good for throughput but add cross-region RTT.
- Hypothesis: a small dedicated reserve in edge POPs will reduce failover RTT and improve tail latency for small interactive requests. Also helps for predictable SLA-backed customers.

2) Sizing rationale
- Baseline traffic patterns (last 30 days): edge POP steady-state small-request concurrency (<=4 tokens/user) is ~18–22 rps peak per POP for our top-10 low-latency customers.
- Target reserve: 6 GPUs provides ~96–120 concurrent small-batch slots assuming our optimized tiny-batching config (16 concurrent streams per GPU for <128 token requests).
- Safety cushion: +25% buffer to avoid immediate preemption during load bursts. That yields 7–8 GPUs; we will start at 6 and scale to 8 if observed contention >10%.

3) Cost estimate (quick math)
- Region unit cost (booked rate): $2.40 / GPU-hour for edge-node VPC flavor (price masked for public doc).
- 6 GPUs * 24h * 7d = 1008 GPU-hours per week. Weekly incremental cost ≈ 1008 * $2.40 ≈ $2.4k per region. Two regions in trial → ~$4.8k/wk. Monthly run rate ≈ $19k. This is ~4–6% increase on current regional spend per region depending on utilization profile.
- Finance: Rina will confirm exact chargeback numbers and whether this fits within Q3 infrastructure contingency.

4) Implementation approach
- Provision as a distinct capacity pool labeled edge-reserve-{region}.
- Autoscale policy: keep min=6, max=8, scale-trigger=manual-schedule + spot-reconciliation job. Prevent dynamic bursting beyond 8 unless a manual override with ops approval.
- Prewarming: run a lightweight synthetic sequence every 90s to keep kernels hot and to prefill warm KV caches (safe warmup load: single 32-token request per GPU).
- Route selection: update smart-routing weight for SLA-tagged customers to prefer edge-reserve pool when available; fallback to regional main pool if not.

5) Observability / metrics to monitor (what success looks like)
- Primary metric: 95p and 99p end-to-end latency for requests <=128 tokens for SLA customers served via the POP. Target: 95p tail improvement >=15% and 99p >=10% within 3 weeks.
- Secondary metrics: reserve pool utilization (target 40–80% in steady-state), prewarm hit rate (percentage of requests that served without kernel cold hits), cross-region failover time reduction.
- Cost guardrails: weekly delta vs baseline and cumulative monthly delta. Auto-alert if weekly delta >8%.

6) Risks and mitigations
- Risk: reserved GPUs sit idle too long → cost leak. Mitigation: reserve-lifecycle job will downscale to min=0 overnight for low-traffic windows (region-specific schedule) after week 1 if utilization <10% for 3 consecutive days. That will require re-approval from product for SLA customers.
- Risk: warmup synthetic traffic impacts other customers if misconfigured. Mitigation: synthetic traffic uses a dedicated internal tenant and strictly capped QPS.
- Risk: complexity in routing rules leading to unexpected hot-paths. Mitigation: staged rollout — start with single customer (pilot) in US-WEST-2, monitor 72 hours, then expand.

7) Decision log entries (who decided what)
- 2027-06-14: Approve pilot (6 GPUs) in US-WEST-2 and EU-CENTRAL-1 for 6-week trial — agreed by infrastructure leads (Amira, Diego) + product (Rina) with SRE nod (Marcus).
- 2027-06-15: Implementation owner assigned — Omar Bennett (infra ops) to create capacity pool and schedule prewarm job; due 2027-06-18.

8) Action items (short list)
- Omar Bennett: provision edge-reserve-USW2 min=6 max=8, schedule prewarm job, create DNS/tagging, and open PR for routing changes. Due: 2027-06-18.
- Rina Patel: confirm finance chargeback and return with exact per-region cost delta and recommended approval channel. Due: 2027-06-17.
- Diego Park: write small runbook (playbook) for reserve pool drain and emergency override steps; include rollback checklist. Due: 2027-06-20.
- Marcus Li: add monitoring panels to edge-sla-metrics dashboard and add alerts for weekly cost delta and 99p latency regression. Due: 2027-06-19.
- Amira Kline: share this decision log with product ops, customer success, and legal (for SLA language) and fold feedback into week-2 review. Due: 2027-06-16.

9) Pilot gating criteria / exit criteria
- Promote from pilot to region-wide policy if after 6 weeks: 95p latency improvement >=15% and monthly cost delta <=6%.
- Rollback if: 95p improvement <5% after 3 weeks OR weekly cost delta spikes above 8% for >1 week.

10) Notes to self / unresolved questions
- Need to check whether current billing metrics capture reserved but idle GPU costs at the level of customer chargeback. Conspicuously different behavior between on-demand and reserved may affect accounting.
- Confirm whether prewarm synthetic can be sampled through tracing without leaking to customer logs.
- We might want a lighter-footprint GPU flavor for reserves in certain POPs — file a follow-up ticket to procurement to explore spot-like micro-instances for edge POPs.

Appendix: quick commands / refs
- Ticket to create pool: JIRA-3145 (infra: create edge reserve pool)
- Routing PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/782
- Perf data query (example): bigquery://infra_edge_latency.edge_small_reqs?filter=region:us-west-2&window=30d

Next sync: standup check-in 2027-06-18 09:30 PT (quick go/no-go), full review 1-week after pilot start (2027-06-25).

Raw brainstorming snippets (work-in-progress)
- "If we can shave 30–40ms off 95p we can justify premium for SLA customers — need to quantify ARR impact."
- "Would love a planner view that shows per-customer per-POP tail latency and inferred cost saving from reserve — might be a product feature idea for optimize team."
- "Consider combining reserve with sticky-routing so warm caches are more likely to be hit for repeat users (session affinity)."

End of doc.
